title: Atezolizumab + nab-paclitaxel

agents.name: Atezolizumab
agents.explanation: Atezolizumab blocks PD-L1 signalling that can restrain immune cells. This may help the immune system attack cancer, but it can also inflame healthy organs. Immune effects can begin during treatment or after it has stopped.
agents.watch: Report new cough, diarrhoea, jaundice, severe rash, unusual weakness, headache, thirst or changes in urination promptly.
risks: Immune inflammation of lungs, bowel, liver or kidneys
Thyroid, adrenal or pituitary problems and diabetes
Rare serious heart, nerve or muscle inflammation
Infusion reactions and severe skin reactions

agents.name: Nab-paclitaxel
agents.mechanism: Disrupts cell division by stabilising microtubules
agents.explanation: This formulation carries paclitaxel with albumin, a protein. It interferes with the structures cells use to divide. Its dosing and allergy precautions differ from ordinary paclitaxel.
agents.watch: Report numbness, tingling, weakness or problems with daily tasks before the next dose. Tell staff about an infusion reaction; new cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment.
risks: Numbness / tingling or weakness, sometimes lasting
Low blood counts, infection and sepsis
Hair loss, fatigue and muscle / joint aches
Infusion reactions; uncommon serious lung inflammation

context_label: Previously untreated unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer with eligible PD-L1 expression
purpose: Control advanced cancer and symptoms while balancing side effects and treatment burden.
schedule_summary: Atezolizumab 840 mg is given on Days 1 and 15, before nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Nab-paclitaxel is planned for up to six cycles; extension needs consultant review. Atezolizumab may continue after chemotherapy stops.

medicines_title: Your medicines and what they do
timeline_note: These broad symptom bands are educational possibilities, not measured risk curves. Infusion days are the planned schedule; delays require a new clinical plan.
safety_note: Fever, shivers, sudden illness, severe breathing changes or chest pain need prompt assessment on any day.
teachback: Which medicines and doses are prescribed, when are they due, which checks are needed, and what would make you call the team today?
consent_support: Discuss the exact setting, expected benefit, alternatives, medicine-specific risks, monitoring, contraception and urgent contact plan.
urgent_extra: Fever, new cough or breathlessness, diarrhoea, severe rash, jaundice, unusual weakness, marked thirst, severe headache or confusion needs prompt advice, including after treatment ends.

support.title: Know the treatment day
support.text: Day 8 is nab-paclitaxel only. Confirm which medicines are due at every visit.

support.title: Immune symptoms
support.text: Report new symptoms promptly, even after treatment ends. Do not assume diarrhoea or breathlessness is an ordinary chemotherapy effect.

support.title: Nerves and blood counts
support.text: Report numbness before the next dose; fever or unusual bleeding needs urgent advice.

support.title: Medicines and vaccines
support.text: Discuss steroids, new medicines and vaccinations with the team.

questions.q: Why was this treatment chosen for me?
questions.a: This combination brings checkpoint immunotherapy together with albumin-bound paclitaxel for a defined first-line triple-negative breast population. The validated PD-L1 test, previous treatment, autoimmune history, organ health and patient priorities affect suitability.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed or missed?
questions.a: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

questions.q: Who arranges the checks and explains the results?
questions.a: Agree the due window, booking team, result reviewer and contact route if a test or appointment is missing. This page does not record completed checks.

questions.q: Can I take other medicines or supplements?
questions.a: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.

items.text: Previously untreated unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer with eligible PD-L1 expression

items.title: Your exact schedule
items.text: Atezolizumab 840 mg is given on Days 1 and 15, before nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle. Nab-paclitaxel is planned for up to six cycles; extension needs consultant review. Atezolizumab may continue after chemotherapy stops.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss biomarker-directed, endocrine, chemotherapy and supportive-care options appropriate to this setting, including the option not to proceed.

chapters.title: Checks across treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and reviews the results before treatment decisions.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: Baseline FBC, kidney/liver function, glucose, thyroid function, hepatitis B/C testing and morning cortisol. FBC, kidney/liver tests and glucose before each cycle; check the count results needed for Day 8 and Day 15 decisions.

items.title: Other treatment-specific checks
items.text: Thyroid function at Cycle 1 Day 1 and every second cycle. Review immune symptoms throughout and after treatment. Cardiac imaging is based on history/prior anthracyclines or clinical concern; there is no routine HER2-style echo schedule.

items.title: Cancer review and follow-up
items.text: Agree the scan type and review interval for the known disease sites. Review response, symptoms and toxicity together; new or worsening symptoms may need an earlier assessment.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-health assessment follows endocrine therapy, ovarian suppression, menopause and other fracture risks. It has its own monitoring plan.

chapters.title: The wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Review response, toxicity and priorities to decide whether to continue, change or stop. Supportive and palliative care can accompany anticancer treatment.

items.title: Treatment changes
items.text: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

items.title: Medicines review
items.text: Check new prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines and supplements with the oncology pharmacist before taking them.

items.title: After treatment
items.text: Keep the agreed follow-up and report persistent or new symptoms between visits.

phases.label: Combination treatment
phases.detail: Atezolizumab Days 1/15 and nab-paclitaxel Days 1/8/15. Review the chemotherapy component after up to six cycles.

phases.label: Atezolizumab continuation if selected
phases.detail: Immunotherapy may continue after nab-paclitaxel stops; immune checks and symptom reporting continue.

steps.title: Before treatment
steps.text: Baseline FBC, kidney/liver function, glucose, thyroid function, hepatitis B/C testing and morning cortisol. FBC, kidney/liver tests and glucose before each cycle; check the count results needed for Day 8 and Day 15 decisions.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. A port is not automatically required; insertion and removal are separate procedures with individual instructions.

steps.title: On the treatment day
steps.text: Atezolizumab is given first, then nab-paclitaxel; Day 8 has nab-paclitaxel only.

steps.title: After the visit
steps.text: No routine take-home infusion pump is required for this regimen. Keep line-care, urgent-contact and next-review instructions.

details.title: Visit length
details.text: Atezolizumab: 60 minutes initially, then 30 minutes if tolerated; nab-paclitaxel: 30 minutes. Full visits also include preparation, review and observation.

details.title: Line care
details.text: A PICC or port has its own care plan. Report fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or line damage; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: Treatment changes
details.text: A delayed, omitted or changed dose needs an updated plan from the treating team. Do not move doses or restart on your own.

details.title: Support for this visit
details.text: Separate combination, Day 8 chemotherapy-only and immunotherapy-only support; maintain immune and blood-count monitoring.

anatomy: New cough or breathlessness may reflect immune inflammation.
Report diarrhoea early, especially pain or blood in stool.
Jaundice or dark urine needs prompt review.
Marked weakness, thirst, headache or dizziness needs assessment.
Fever, bruising or sudden illness: contact oncology.
Report numbness or tingling before another dose.
